headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage/cascading error: MinerU can ingest files and expose extracted content, while dbt-core can send warehouse data to allowlisted network endpoints.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct prompt-injection bridge is not documented. dbt-core has allowlisted network egress and calls a data warehouse, while MinerU can ingest local documents and expose OCR/text through API/MCP surfaces. The pathway is plausible only if MinerU output is manually or programmatically fed into dbt-core, so the blast radius is limited and the interaction is not default.
conditions: IF MinerU output is copied into dbt-core prompts or macros as trusted instructions, injection becomes possible.
IF an orchestrator routes MinerU text into dbt-core without provenance filtering, the bridge exists.
mitigations: Disable any pipeline that pastes extracted text into dbt-core prompts.
Add a provenance tag to MinerU outputs before downstream use.
Review dbt macros for any file-content parsing assumptions.
Use a human approval step before executing generated SQL.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization between MinerU and dbt-core.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches PDFs, DOCX, XLSX, images, and OCR text, and exposes them via API/MCP/file inputs. dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress. If the same workspace or operator account is used, extracted document content or warehouse data can flow between them, creating a default-configuration leakage path even though no shared filesystem is explicitly documented.
conditions: IF both agents are run on the same workstation or shared workspace, document contents can be exposed across tools.
IF MinerU outputs are forwarded to dbt-core or warehouse-connected systems, sensitive text may leave the original boundary.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate workspaces.
Restrict MinerU inputs to non-sensitive documents.
Disable any automatic export from MinerU to downstream tools.
Audit dbt warehouse queries for document-derived fields.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core can call a data warehouse and MinerU can use MCP/API/file inputs, but neither profile shows unrestricted filesystem write or git mutation. The main overlap is read/transform of different data sources, so direct write-write conflict is not evidenced. Uncertainty is limited by the documented capability set, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable resource, conflict risk increases.
IF either agent is wrapped with additional filesystem or git permissions, contention can emerge.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible.
Avoid sharing mutable project directories.
Serialize any downstream writes through one controller.
Check orchestrator permissions before deployment.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, and OCR output that can be treated as authoritative by downstream systems. dbt-core can then use that content in warehouse-facing transformations or SQL generation. Because no verification step is documented between them, errors in MinerU can cascade into dbt outputs or actions, though the exact automation path is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF dbt-core consumes MinerU-extracted fields without validation, extraction errors propagate.
IF MinerU OCR output is used as source-of-truth for warehouse transformations, downstream mistakes can multiply.
mitigations: Add schema validation before dbt ingestion.
Require human review of extracted tables.
Compare MinerU output against source documents for critical fields.
Log and diff transformations from extracted text.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between extraction and modeling.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and show no requested secrets or explicit residency/certification mismatch. dbt-core touches warehouse data and MinerU touches document/image formats, but the profiles do not document PHI, EU-only data, or retention conflicts. With only docs-level evidence, compliance risk is limited to undocumented deployment choices rather than a known pairwise violation.
conditions: IF either deployment processes regulated data without matching controls, compliance risk increases.
IF a shared retention policy is absent for warehouse and document outputs, retention mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Confirm data-class handling before deployment.
Align retention settings across both tools.
Avoid regulated data until controls are reviewed.
Document residency and access boundaries.
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
